A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe Instant Policy. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–J are readable and directly comparable, with no material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-world experiments, including task success rates, ablations, scaling results and object-generalisation evaluations in Tables 1–4 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including simulation, real-world evaluation, ablations and qualitative transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The graph representation, diffusion objective, network architecture, action prediction and downstream adaptations are unchanged. The added training information does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ShapeNet-based pseudo-demonstrations, 24 RLBench tasks, 16 real-world tasks, four novel-object tasks and transfer scenarios. The newly disclosed trajectory count does not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain the same adapted BC-Z, Vid2Robot and GPT2 comparators. Their documented adaptations and participation in the comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated evaluation defaults, training budgets, rollout counts and RLBench restrictions are retained. v2 newly specifies training-context randomisation between one and five demonstrations; v1 did not explicitly fix the training-context count, so this is additional disclosure rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: Table 2 ablations, Figure 6 scaling analyses, object-generalisation tests and Appendices G–H failure and design-choice analyses are unchanged. Figure 5 redisplays the same attention evidence without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: The rollout counts and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds training-seed information, repeated-training summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, scaling curves and qualitative findings retain the same results. For example, Instant Policy remains at 0.71 average success with pseudo-demonstrations alone in Table 1 and 88.75% real-world success in Table 3. Figure 5 retains the same attention plots and task snapshots.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, graph definitions, diffusion equations and action-recovery derivation are unchanged, including Equations 1–6 and the appendix explanations. No proofs or formal assumptions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: immediate imitation from few demonstrations, graph diffusion, training with pseudo-demonstrations, generalisation and downstream transfer.

C2.justification: Interpretations of attention, scaling, generalisation and transfer remain unchanged. Section 5 limitations and Appendix G failure explanations are identical; the revised figure labels do not introduce a new scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly states that pseudo-demonstrations are generated in parallel, that training corresponds to roughly 700K unique trajectories, and that training contexts contain a randomised one to five demonstrations. These details were absent from v1, including its appendices. Other implementation and access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and positioning relative to previous imitation-learning, diffusion and graph-network research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental-setup paragraph is lightly rewritten and expanded, with isolated wording edits elsewhere. The section order and narrative structure remain intact. A small grammatical regression changes 'a large margin' to 'a large margins'.

P2.justification: Figure 5 reorganises labels and demonstration grouping, adds visual connections to task snapshots, and replaces timestep labels with task-stage descriptions. Figure 8 changes its caption from demonstration order to usage stage. These are local presentation edits; the underlying plots, images and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added trajectory estimate and training-context range in Section 4 reduce ambiguity about reproducing the training setup. Figure 5 also makes the relationship between attention and task stages clearer. These provide modest documentation and readability gains, while the scientific evidence, claims and limitations remain unchanged.
